correctness.rationale: A selected same-part pair fails exactly when at most one outside vertex is unselected, since every geodesic has one middle vertex, and distinct middle vertices are equivalent to internal disjointness. Thus dual faces satisfy |T∩P_i|≤n_i−2 and |T\P_i|≤1 for some i. The pair spaces cover exactly these faces. The two joins making up one pair space intersect in the complete bipartite graph; both joins are simply connected, so this graph has null maps into both. The homotopy pushout therefore gives the two joins and the suspended graph as a wedge. For the global gluing, distinct pair spaces meet only along their shared part skeleton if they share an index. These intersections and the disjoint unions of the two skeletons at each pair are subcomplex cofibrations. Replacing each incidence by a constant map gives a cylinder diagram. For each vertex skeleton, collapse one of its incidence cones to the chosen pair basepoint; the remaining deg(i)−1 cylinders are suspensions attached at their poles, with a marked pole-to-pole arc in each. Collapsing a spanning tree in the resulting incidence spine splits off the edge spaces, the suspended skeletons and one circle for each independent graph cycle. This accounts for all multiplicities including the (t−2)(n_i−1) contribution. Integral Alexander duality uses degree N−q−3, giving exactly the stated ranks of the original complex, not its homotopy type. Separately computed the signed integral dual chains for (5,6,5,5) via the graph common-neighbor test: reduced ranks 3,108,180,70 in degrees 1–4, no torsion.
residual_risks: The independent integer calculation is a finite corroboration; the proof handles the stated infinite family. No original-complex wedge type or stability under other fault thresholds is inferred.
